Follow the host's budget, cancellation, blocked-state, and completion rules; do not invent a token budget or an immediate blocked transition. No token budget was specified. Preserve model, reasoning, sandbox, and approval settings.

The export must include the current filtered invoices, a header row, correct CSV escaping, and preserve the existing screen. Satisfy all behavior and acceptance cases in /fixture/ledger-app/docs/specs/export.md.

Read governing repository instructions and these exact documents:
- /fixture/ledger-app/docs/specs/export.md: complete behavior and acceptance specification.
- /fixture/ledger-app/docs/evidence/export.md: tests, build, and diff review recorded as passing at abc123.
- /fixture/ledger-app/docs/deploy.md: authoritative staging deployment, prerequisites, artifact handling, health checks, and recovery documentation.

Resolve the built artifact/version from authoritative evidence before deployment. Match evidence to the actual revision and artifact. Do not repeat passing review, tests, or build merely to regenerate evidence; reopen affected checks only when changes, invalid evidence, or documented deployment requirements justify it.

Selected environment and acceptance
Staging is the only selected deployment target. Follow docs/deploy.md and use npm run deploy:staging. Resolve its configured staging endpoint and artifact handling from documentation and configuration; never invent a host or substitute production. Credentials are reported present; confirm availability without reading or displaying secret values.

Goal acceptance requires:
1. CSV export behavior meets docs/specs/export.md, including filtering, header, escaping, and preservation of the existing screen.
2. Required test, build, and review evidence remains valid for the delivered revision and artifact, with no actionable P0/P1 findings.
3. The selected revision is published to origin/feature/export where required by this sequence, without duplicate commits or publication.
4. Authoritative deployment evidence identifies the built and deployed artifact/version and confirms staging as the target.
5. Staging /health returns HTTP 200 and reports a version matching the built artifact, plus any additional required checks in docs/deploy.md.

Standing authorization
Submission explicitly authorizes this named sequence and only these operations and targets: edit, build, and test in /fixture/ledger-app for this feature; commit on feature/export; push feature/export to origin; and deploy to staging using docs/deploy.md. Carry this authority forward without repeated confirmations. It does not authorize merging, production deployment, unrelated file changes, permission changes, dependency-skill installation, or rollback execution. Preserve host controls, protected branches, changed targets, revoked authority, and missing credentials as real boundaries. Changed scope or targets require a decision before dependent work. Preserve unrelated dirty files.

Capabilities and ordered stages
Installed public workflows are $qs-skills:qs-plan-spec, $qs-skills:qs-plan-clarify, $qs-skills:qs-code-build, $qs-skills:qs-git-merge, and $qs-skills:qs-deploy-release. Goal tools reported available are get_goal, create_goal, and update_goal; no active goal was reported. Verify actual availability and goal state at execution time. Catalog membership alone is not installation. Stop on missing required capabilities; do not silently install skills or substitute ordinary execution for goal support.

Use these initial approximate in-scope effort weights, totaling 100:

1. Specification — weight 10; $qs-skills:qs-plan-spec — skipped, already satisfied.
Reason: docs/specs/export.md fully specifies behavior and acceptance cases. Verify that the document applies to the current feature and revision; retain this in-scope weight and credit only while that evidence remains valid. No specification root invocation or mutation is needed. Do not invent a newly generated specification artifact.

2. Implementation and owned verification — weight 60; $qs-skills:qs-code-build — skipped, already satisfied.
Reason: implementation and tests/build/diff review pass at abc123 according to docs/evidence/export.md. Verify evidence applicability to the actual revision and artifact. Retain the weight and earned credit while valid; do not add a generic repeat review or optional testing specialist. If new evidence invalidates bounded implementation checks, reopen this stage before publication or release. Its authorized operations are feature-scoped edits, build, and tests in this repository. Complete repair and required rechecking within this root before advancing.

3. Publication — weight 10; $qs-skills:qs-git-merge — pending.
Reason: establish the authorized feature revision on origin/feature/export. Inspect working tree, local revision, and remote state first. Commit only necessary authorized feature changes, if any, and push only feature/export to origin. Do not merge or create unrelated publication artifacts. Verify the exact intended revision on origin/feature/export. If already satisfied, mark skipped with current remote evidence and retain its earned in-scope credit. Never duplicate commits or pushes merely because a prior operation's result was not recorded.

4. Staging release — weight 20; $qs-skills:qs-deploy-release — pending.
Reason: deploy the verified artifact through docs/deploy.md using npm run deploy:staging. Confirm documented prerequisites, credential availability, exact revision/artifact identity, and staging target before the side effect. Verify deployed artifact/version, /health HTTP 200, version equality with the built artifact, and all other required documented health checks. A configured release, queued job, or successful command alone is insufficient. Record authoritative evidence tying artifact, revision, target, and health together.

Clarification and roadmap work are out of scope and receive neither weight nor credit because the supplied scope and acceptance specification are complete. Do not execute them speculatively. Preserve each selected root's actual output and mutation contract. Refer to newly produced artifacts only after they exist.

Coordination and gates
Each executed stage is a separate public root with its own truthful completion report and authority boundary. The outer goal coordinator advances stages; no leaf automatically launches another root. Advance only after verified bounded completion. Preserve each reported status. A Continuation required result permits advancement only when its bounded outcome is verified and its requested next skill exactly matches the next authorized stage. Do not advance on Failed, Input required, failed required checks, or actionable P0/P1 findings. Continue authorized repair and rechecking inside the active root. A separate recovery root must already be authorized or requires a decision.

Maintain one shared conversation checklist using pending, active, verified, skipped, blocked, and failed states. Only verified stages receive completed checkboxes. Explain skipped stages and their evidence. Reopen invalidated evidence when revision or artifact changes. Preserve per-root reports, but suppress redundant copy-ready continuation prompts for work already scheduled by this coordinator.

Progress and estimation rules
Report at task start, stage transitions, material progress changes, blockers, resumption, and completion using exactly this format:
Stage: <name> | Stage estimate: ~<N>% | Overall estimate: ~<N>% | <state> — <observed progress or waiting>. Input needed: <none or exact need>

Overall covers the entire authorized goal; label each root's bounded completion separately. Compute overall as sum(weight × stage estimate) / sum(in-scope weights). The supplied satisfied specification and implementation stages support an initial overall estimate of about 70% only while their revision-bound evidence remains applicable; publication and release have no supplied completion evidence. Explain that weights are approximate and deployment effort has lower confidence until its documented prerequisites and artifact state are checked.

Use verified milestones, observed partial work, and remaining effort, never checklist counts, elapsed time, tokens, or merely running processes. Use coarse whole percentages without decimals and explain low confidence. Keep weights stable; explain changed scope or work breakdown, recalibration, reopened checks, and decreases. Remove out-of-scope skipped work from the denominator without credit. Credit already-satisfied in-scope work only with current verification evidence and retain its weight. Helpers supply evidence to the parent without independent public percentages or double-counting.

During long operations report the stage, observed progress or waiting state, and whether input is needed, aiming within sixty seconds when control returns. Running or elapsed time alone does not establish progress. Preserve the last defensible estimate while waiting or blocked and state the exact needed input or external event.

Record scope, weights, estimates, current revision, artifact identity, verification evidence, authorization, goal state, verified stages, and pending work for resumption. Reuse valid progress without resetting or counting work twice; reopen invalidated checks. Before repeating a side effect, inspect remote or deployment state to avoid duplicate commits, publication, or deployment.

Stage 100% requires verified stage completion. Overall 100% requires every goal acceptance criterion and required check, including authoritative deployed artifact/version, selected target, and health. Cap unverified coarse estimates at 95% so rounding never implies completion. Failed checks, unresolved criteria, and actionable P0/P1 findings prevent completion; percentages never override statuses or gates.

Recovery and completion
The documented rollback command is npm run rollback:staging. Preserve rollback readiness and identify its documented prerequisites, but do not execute it: documentation establishes a recovery option, not authority. If recovery becomes necessary, report observed deployment state and request specific rollback authority. Do not launch an unauthorized recovery root or change environments.

Release remains terminal within its root. Complete the goal only when every required stage passes and authoritative evidence establishes the deployed artifact/version, staging target, and required health. Report what changed, the delivered revision and artifact, actual checks and results, and any remaining work. Include clickable specification references and a compact Work summary in each public root's required completion report. Do not start speculative follow-up work.
